name: DDRK (Dance Dance Revolution Keyboard)
tagline: A foot-operated keyboard: step dance-game patterns to type letters while staying active.
problem: Students and workers sit for hours at keyboards; the team wanted typing that keeps the body moving.
solution: A plywood pad with buttons on a microcontroller; step combinations map to characters, and a Python layer sends them to the computer as keystrokes.
demo_moment: Team-described: type a word by stepping out patterns on the pad.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Turns a childhood rhythm game into an input device.
A physical pad judges can stand on is a strong hardware-prize demo.

lessons: For a hardware prize, a sturdy device people can use in the room beats a complex one that wobbles.
